interludes.speaker: cook
interludes.text: Chef Marco found the extra food crate we packed on Earth. Stretch it out, or cook a big Moon feast?
interludes.fact: Astronauts often eat tortillas instead of bread, because crumbs floating around can get into equipment.

interludes.speaker: eng
interludes.text: The water pump is wheezing. We packed spare parts on Earth. Build a new pump now?
interludes.fact: The space station keeps spare parts on board and sends more by cargo ship, because the nearest repair shop is 400 km down.

interludes.speaker: ls
interludes.text: Cabin pressure is dropping very slowly. Remember the hull trouble from launch? Hunt for the leak, or top up the air?
interludes.fact: Space station crews have hunted tiny air leaks with ultrasonic detectors that hear the hiss we can't.

interludes.speaker: arch
interludes.text: Our ridge gets sunlight almost nonstop. Add extra solar panels to use every ray?
interludes.fact: Some peaks near the lunar south pole are in sunlight for more than 80% of the year.

interludes.speaker: sci
interludes.text: The ancient ice is steps from our front door. Drill a core sample?

variants.text: The ancient ice is steps from our door, and our extra science rack can analyze it. Drill a core sample?

interludes.fact: Ice in permanently shadowed craters can be billions of years old, like a frozen diary of the solar system.

interludes.speaker: med
interludes.text: Dr. Silva wants a check-up for everyone who skipped the shelter during that solar flare. It takes a day.
interludes.fact: Astronauts wear small badges that measure their radiation dose, so doctors can keep track.
